questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Whether food allergies are more common now, and why
How to cook tasty meals without using any peanuts
The difference between nuts and legumes in cooking
How to treat eczema in babies with special creams
questions.why: Neil says the topic is whether there are more food allergies these days.

questions.q: Which foods does Rob mention that can cause allergies?
options: Bread, rice and pasta
Peanuts, shellfish and milk
Fruit and vegetables
Chocolate and sugar
questions.why: He mentions peanuts, shellfish, milk and so on.

questions.q: Who in Neil's family has a food allergy?
options: Neil himself
His wife
His daughter
His son
questions.why: He says his daughter is allergic to tree nuts.

questions.q: How sure is Dr Adam Fox that allergies have increased?
options: Not at all sure
He thinks it's only in the news more
He says there is no clear evidence
Very confident, based on strong studies
questions.why: He says 'we can be very confident', and robust studies show significant increases.

questions.q: Over what period does Dr Fox say the studies show increases?
options: The last 2 or 3 years
Around 20 or 30 years
Over 100 years
Since the Second World War
questions.why: He says studies show significant increases 'over 20, 30 years'.

questions.q: What does Dr Fox say about genetics?
options: It is the main cause of the rise in allergies
It explains about half of the increase
The increase can't be explained by genetics
It causes eczema but not food allergies
questions.why: He says, 'We certainly can't put it down to genetics.'

questions.q: What link does Dr Fox describe?
options: Babies with eczema are more likely to get a food allergy
Eating peanuts too early in life causes eczema in babies
Adults with food allergies often get eczema later in life
Eczema actually protects young children from allergies
questions.why: He says there's a direct relationship between eczema in infancy and getting a food allergy.

questions.q: What does Rob mean by saying Neil is 'allergic to hard work'?
options: Neil often gets ill at work when he's busy
Neil works too much and never takes a break
Neil has a real allergy to office dust
He's joking Neil avoids explaining legumes
questions.why: He says it after Neil refuses to explain why a peanut isn't a nut.
